title: Rest in Christ
definition: Rest in Christ is the believer's trustful relief from striving, condemnation, anxiety, and self-salvation through the finished work and gentle care of Jesus.
summary: Rest in Christ is the soul's ceasing from self-salvation, anxious striving, and burdensome self-rule by trusting Jesus.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is gentle and lowly in heart, giving rest to those burdened by sin and weakness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Rest in Christ is the soul's relief from striving for acceptance, carrying guilt alone, and living under crushing burdens. Scripture presents Jesus as the One who gives rest to the weary.

This rest is not laziness or escape from obedience. It is the deep rest of coming to Christ, receiving His yoke, and learning from Him as a gentle and lowly Savior.

Jesus gives rest because He has finished the saving work sinners could never complete. His lordship does not crush His people; it restores them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people are exhausted by performance, shame, disability, recovery battles, caregiving, ministry pressure, or trying to prove they are enough. Rest in Christ speaks directly to burdened souls.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to Christ with the burdens you keep trying to carry alone. Receive His finished work, order your life under His gentle rule, and practice rhythms of prayer, worship, and trust instead of constant striving.
